title: Strong Symmetry from Two-Point Correlations
abstract: Strong and weak symmetries and their spontaneous breaking distinguish different forms of symmetry and order in mixed states. We show that complete one- and two-point correlation functions, equivalently all two-site reduced density matrices, determine exact strong symmetry for continuous onsite unitary actions of connected groups: states with identical correlations have the same strong symmetry and character. We also present an algorithm to determine the maximal connected strong-symmetry sub-Lie group and its character from two-point correlations. Because such correlations are more accessible than full-state tomography, the algorithm is readily applicable to experiments ranging from condensed-matter systems to quantum simulators and circuits. We also identify group and representation-specific cases in which fewer correlations suffice.
summary: This theoretical work establishes that the strong symmetry of a mixed quantum state can be fully determined by measuring only its two-point correlation functions. By analyzing the covariance matrix derived from these correlations, the authors provide an algorithm to identify the maximal symmetry subgroup and its associated character. This is highly valuable because low-order correlations are more accessible experimentally than full state tomography.
main_problem: The paper addresses how to determine the exact 'strong symmetry' of a mixed quantum state using only low-order correlation functions, circumventing the need for full-state tomography.
main_result: It proves that for continuous onsite unitary actions of connected groups, identical two-point correlations are sufficient to determine the state's strong symmetry and its associated character.
method: The method involves analyzing the charge covariance matrix derived from one- and two-point correlation functions to identify the generators of the maximal connected strong-symmetry subgroup.
model_or_system: The theory applies to general quantum many-body systems ($N$ sites) whose symmetries are governed by a connected topological group $G$ acting via onsite unitary representations.
key_observables: One- and two-point correlation functions, two-site reduced density matrices ($ho_{ij}$), and the charge covariance matrix $\Gamma(ho)$.
important_parameters: The continuous nature of the symmetry group $G$ and the requirement of onsite unitary actions.
main_assumptions: The results are rigorously proven only for continuous onsite unitary actions of connected groups; the method fails for discrete symmetries.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates that selected two-site data can establish strong symmetry, even when some pairs are unmeasured.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical equivalence between equal two-point correlations and equal pair RDMs (Theorem 1), then provides a constructive algorithm (Theorem 2) using the covariance kernel to find the maximal symmetry subgroup $H_ho$ and its character $\chi_ho$.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, experimentally accessible diagnostic tool for characterizing symmetry in complex quantum many-body systems, directly relevant to understanding symmetry breaking in correlated materials.
